facts.detail: The checker presents coverage for EE, Vodafone, O2 and Three, the four main UK mobile network operators.
Ofcom uses Ordnance Survey data for the property dataset shown by the mobile checker.
The checker property dataset is updated three times a year.
Ofcom states that its mobile coverage API uses the same data that powers the checker.
The coverage map is based on operator predictions generated by programs simulating signal travel and obstruction.

facts.detail: Operator coverage predictions are processed into a 50 metre by 50 metre grid covering the UK land mass.
Ofcom tests predictions in the real world using dedicated measurement hardware at a sample of UK locations.
Ofcom says model predictions are generally reliable but cannot guarantee coverage at a specific location.
Ofcom aims to refresh mobile coverage information every three months or in line with Connected Nations publications.
Ofcom warns that trees, buildings and seasonal foliage can cause local differences from average grid predictions.

facts.detail: Ofcom published its one-million-user Map Your Mobile update on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used the Map Your Mobile checker.
The service uses a postcode to map which mobile networks are available in the local area.
The checker provides a performance score for networks at postal-district level.
Ofcom says the checker combines Opensignal crowdsourced real-experience data with predictive information from mobile networks.

facts.detail: Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, or 82% of homes, in the January 2026 snapshot.
Ofcom reports 1.2 million additional homes gained full-fibre access in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million connections, equal to 47% of premises with access.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 27.1 million homes, or 89%.
Ofcom reports 4,000 premises without affordable decent broadband and 39,000 unable to receive decent service from fixed line or fixed wireless access.

facts.detail: Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from all mobile network operators reached 84% of UK landmass.
Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from at least one operator remained at 96% of UK landmass.
All four operators maintained predicted 4G coverage outside at least 99% of UK premises.
Outside-premises 5G standalone coverage ranged from 49% to 85% across the three operators that had deployed it.
Overall outside-premises 5G coverage from all operators increased from 47% to 64%.
